title: Velocity & Resilience: Town Hall and Strategy Check
topics: Product focus: latency, cost, Dedicated/Private uptake
EMEA region expansion and data residency
summary: Leadership presents a compact strategy update focused on balancing velocity (feature delivery) with operational resilience. We discussed targeted hiring, cost-saving levers in Redwood Optimize, Dedicated customer momentum, and a new EMEA compliance enrollment plan. There was a candid Q&A about timelines, SLAs, and tradeoffs between hosted vs private deployments.
action_items: Priya Singh: Publish Q3 product roadmap one-pager (due: 2026-08-06)
Sofia Ramos: Share updated on-call rotation and incident runbook link (due: 2026-08-03)
Daniel Wu: Provide updated headcount forecast and hiring priorities doc (due: 2026-08-05)
Security Team: Post SOC2 progress checklist and EMEA data residency plan (due: 2026-08-10)
Growth: Run cohort-level cost regression for top 10 paying customers (due: 2026-08-12)
next_steps: Read the roadmap one-pager when posted
Leads to review hiring prioritization doc
Schedule small-group deep dives for Dedicated customer playbook
All engineers encouraged to join resilience guild kickoff next week
transcript:
[00:00] Host (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're about to kick off. Mic checks — I see a lot of faces. Um, quick housekeeping, recording is on. We're aiming to keep this to about an hour.
[00:28] Maya: Ok first slide— velocity and resilience, we want to set expectations for Q3. Quick topline: prioritize four initiatives, right? latency, dedicated scale, EMEA compliance, and cost controls.
[01:05] Jonah: I'll take latency and runtime improvements — we shipped some kernel optimizations last sprint that are live in staging. Early numbers look promising, but there are edge cases with long-context KV cache invalidation.
[01:47] Sofia: On the ops side, we've seen two incidents last month, both related to autoscaler misconfig when burst capacity triggered. We're tightening thresholds and adding more circuit breakers.
[02:15] Audience (someone off-mic): Any plan for SLOs on Dedicated?
[02:22] Maya: Yes, Dedicated customers will get firmed SLOs. Daniel will cover financial implications later.
[02:36] Daniel: Finance view — we need to reconcile growth with margin pressure. Headcount is our largest lever. We're not doing a broad freeze, but reprioritizing hiring and pausing non-essential roles until end of Q3. This is to fund Dedicated expansion and EMEA compliance.
[03:10] Priya: For product, the roadmap is tighter: shipping streaming reliability, Optimize prescriptive profiles, and a simpler private deployment quickstart. We'll ship the one-pager by next week.
[03:40] Jonah: Quick technical aside — we're testing a new quantization profile to reduce memory pressure for 8k contexts; the tradeoff is a small QA-detected degradation on hallucination metrics, so we need eval gating.
[04:12] Crowd murmur / brief crosstalk
[04:30] Maya: Transparency note — we will share the eval dashboards. We're not going to sacrifice quality for raw token cost.
[04:46] Arjun: People update: hiring reprioritization means managers should reconfirm offers in flight by Friday. We'll support transitions where roles are paused. Also, slack channel #resilience-guild is open; join if you'd like to help.
[05:15] Question (engineering): Will the Dedicated SKU pricing change?
[05:23] Daniel: We'll keep base pricing stable for committed customers; new customers may see adjusted tiers that reflect burst capacity costs. We'll publish details with Product and Sales.
[05:45] Maya: Ok moving to incidents and learnings — Sofia, you want to walk through root cause?
[05:52] Sofia: Sure — incident A was an autoscaler runaway due to a telemetry spike from one shard. The scaler interpreted the tail latency increase as sustained and spun up GPUs, which later caused knock-on cold-starts. Fixes: rate-limit scaler triggers, add anomaly detection, and add a fallback to narrower model variants.
[06:35] Listener (someone): Did the fallback to smaller model variants cause customer-visible regressions?
[06:40] Sofia: A few customers saw higher latency while we rolled back; we introduced automatic fallback policies soon after. We're expanding the canary window to catch this earlier.
[06:58] Maya: Quick polling — who has been on-call for infra in last two weeks? (several hands) thank you. Helps to acknowledge effort; we'll get a spot award list out.
[07:20] Priya: On Dedicated and Private uptake — the sales team has five active pilots where customers specifically ask for VPC + on-prem options for compliance. These are medium-to-large ARR opportunities but require SOC2 artifacts and a clear private deployment quickstart.
[07:46] Sales rep (Tom): Confirming — pipeline is healthy. Biggest asks are: audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations, and a straightforward billing model for reserved capacity.
[08:10] Daniel: From finance angle, reserved capacity is attractive because it smooths revenue. We plan to offer a committed discount for 6/12 month Dedicated contracts with clear overage rules.
[08:33] Q (CS): Any changes to data retention policy for private deployments?
[08:39] Security lead (Ana): For private we follow customer's retention config; for hosted we plan to offer a short-term retention tier and a separate option for long-retain with additional fees. We'll post the matrix.
[09:10] Audience discussion and small interruptions
[09:30] Jonah: Performance roadmap high-level: kernel selection improvements, optimized softmax for long sequences, and better GPU memory reclamation. Target: 10-15% token cost reduction for typical chats by end of Q3 with no perceptible change to quality.
[10:05] Maya: Ok quick poll — is everyone comfortable with the Q3 bet? Raise in chat if concerns. (chat fills with emoji)
[10:25] Staffer: Request for clearer PR review expectations — cross-team latency changes require runway for testing.
[10:35] Sofia: We'll update the engineering playbook to add a cross-team latency signoff for infra-impacting PRs.
[10:50] Priya: Product experiments: rolling out Optimize recommendations to a subset of customers — it's showing up to 18% savings when prefix caching is enabled and batching tuned. Caveat: requires some prompt engineering to avoid prompt fragmentation.
[11:20] Q (support): How will we communicate runtime changes to customers?
[11:28] Maya: We'll use the status page and per-route release notes in Console. Also plan to send summaries for dedicated customers.
[11:45] Jonah: We also will add a model-variant compatibility table to the Console so teams can see fallback latency and quality tradeoffs.
[12:10] Rapid Q&A — short, shouted questions, some cross-talk
[12:40] Daniel: Budget details — we will reallocate unspent marketing dollars to compliance and sales engineering headcount to accelerate Dedicated deals. Ads will be throttled in Q3.
[13:05] Maya: People-first note — we're committed to minimizing layoffs, but there will be some role pauses. Managers should be transparent with ICs. Arjun will host office hours for questions.
[13:30] Arjun: Office hours schedule posted in #all-hands follow-up. Confidential Q&A form is open.
[13:50] Priya: EMEA strategy — compliance enrollment: step one is SOC2 completion, step two is EEA data residency roadmap with our cloud partners, step three is localized sales enablement. We're targeting first EMEA-ready customers in mid-Q4.
[14:20] Security (Ana): EEA data residency requires region-specific logging and support for in-region KMS. We're aligning with cloud partners on availability windows; there are some lead times for certs.
[14:50] Emergency crosstalk: someone typed "deploy issue" — brief pause while ops confirms
[15:10] Sofia: Ops update — small rollout issue, not customer-impacting, fixed. Back to town hall.
[15:30] Longer Q&A session opens up — employees ask about career ladders, internal mobility, and reprioritization
[17:02] Maya: We want to reward cross-functional contributions, so we'll accelerate visibility for people who contribute to resilience guild.
[17:30] Employee (engineering): Will there be a change to on-call comp?
[17:35] Daniel: We're reviewing recognition and comp for on-call — details in the HR doc.
[18:05] Employee (sales): When will sales get the Dedicated pricing sheet?
[18:10] Tom: We'll circulate a draft by Monday.
[18:30] Rapid-fire updates from each leadership area — product, eng, finance, people, sales — around 30s each
[25:15] Priya: Experiment note — function/tool-calling support is getting more requests; we're going to bake better structured output patterns to reduce post-processing cost.
[25:45] Jonah: Also looking at smarter routing: route requests by cost policy first, latency policy second, but with per-customer overrides. We're adding a routing debug view in Console.
[26:20] Sophia (sic): (laughter, someone mis-says Sofia) small banter
[26:40] Discussion continues — employees interrupt for clarifications; natural speech patterns with small transcription errors like "KV cache" sometimes rendered as "K V cash"
[28:00] Q (product): How tightly are we coupling rollout of Optimize features and runtime changes?
[28:05] Priya: We'll gate Optimize recommendations with a canary and dark traffic tests; runtime changes need separate rollback paths.
[28:30] Marketplace question (financial): Any plan to list on cloud marketplaces?
[28:36] Daniel: Yes, exploring marketplace listing as a channel — timing TBD but likely in Q4 for EMEA and NA.
[29:10] Maya: Closing remarks: be candid, share feedback, and join the resilience guild. We'll have pulse surveys next week. Thanks for your energy.
[29:30] Quick applause (audio faint)
[29:40] Post-meeting smaller breakout — leadership stays for extra 40 minutes for a deeper finance and hiring Q&A.
[30:00] [DEEP DIVE - leadership only]
[30:04] Daniel: Detailed headcount numbers — asks and freezes, we're keeping engineering hiring at modest levels to support Dedicated but pausing some new roles in marketing and ops.
[31:00] Jonah: Technical hires prioritized: runtime, infra reliability, and performance engineers. We also want one senior infra lead focused on autoscaler reliability.
[32:20] Priya: Product hires: one PM for Optimize, one for Dedicated onboarding, one for EMEA compliance enablement.
[33:05] Daniel: If we reallocate marketing budget we can fund two SE hires for next quarter to accelerate Dedicated pilots.
[34:00] Sofia: On-call changes: we'll move to 8-week rotations for infra leads to reduce burnout.
[34:40] Arjun: We'll brief managers on transitioning offers and support packages for impacted candidates.
[35:15] Leadership small-group Q&A continues with more blunt questions and direct answers, a few long pauses and real human emotion.
[52:00] Leadership closes deep dive, thanks team, final reminders about follow-ups and docs.
[52:18] Maya: Ok wrap — roadmap one-pager, hiring doc, SOC2 checklist, and resilience guild invite — please look for those in your inbox.
[52:40] Meeting end — recording stops.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcript had occasional mis-heard acronyms (e.g., KV cache -> K V cash), occasional speaker mislabels, and some sentence fragmentation from overlapping talk.
